cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Reverse the Score
cards.instruction: Turn each apparent loss into a new category of victory, then invite comparison on those changing terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Follow me back to the car. Last in the race, first to spot the kingfisher.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was first to finish. It was a race.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You keep the medal. How many birds did you notice on the way?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was watching the finish line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I win for range, then. You set the pace back; I'll point out everything you missed.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads the return and reverses last-place into bird spotting; A3 concedes medal, A5 yields pace to keep B company while claiming broader attention.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 actual victory causes A3 bird-count comparison; B4 narrow finish focus causes A5 range claim and guided return.

relationship.evidence: B2 defends genuine race achievement and B4 explains why bird watching was not a priority.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 successful focus lose on breadth of observation while giving B real control of the return pace.
